title: Making Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Robust to Irrelevant Context
authors: Ori Yoran and Tomer Wolfson and Ori Ram and Jonathan Berant
benchmark_or_task: Google Search & ColBERTv2 retrievers; Llama-2-13B/70B generators; Self-Ask multi-hop
metrics_reported_or_relevant: EM, F1, order-of-magnitude accuracy on NQ, 2WikiMQA, Bamboogle, StrategyQA, Fermi
actual_contribution: ICLR 2024; NLI-based filtering + finetuning on mixed relevant/irrelevant contexts for RALM robustness
human_supports_claims: Retrieval augmentation can degrade RALM performance when retrieved contexts are irrelevant, especially in multi-hop reasoning where errors cascade. | NLI-based filtering with a back-off to no-retrieval generation is an effective training-free method to mitigate harm from irrelevant evidence, but it over-discards relevant passages. | Fine-tuning with a small mixture of relevant and irrelevant retrieved contexts (as few as 1,000 examples) yields RALMs robust to noisy retrieval while preserving gains from useful evidence.
human_rationale: The paper provides a systematic analysis of RALM brittleness to irrelevant retrieved context across five ODQA benchmarks (including multi-hop) and proposes two complementary remedies: an NLI-based filter with back-off and a data-efficient fine-tuning recipe mixing relevant and noisy contexts. Both contributions directly target the survey's core themes of unreliable evidence robustness, model evidence use, and action control via abstention/back-off. Publication at ICLR 2024 with released code, data, and models makes it a backbone reference for the model-side handling of unreliable retrieval, suitable for the main model-use section.
human_caveat: Experiments are limited to ODQA with Llama-2-13B/70B and small training sets; generalization to other modalities, domains, or larger retrieval corpora is not fully established.

title: SeCon-RAG: A Two-Stage Semantic Filtering and Conflict-Free Framework for Trustworthy RAG
authors: Xiaonan Si and Meilin Zhu and Simeng Qin and Lijia Yu and Lijun Zhang and Shuaitong Liu and Xinfeng Li and Ranjie Duan and Yang Liu and Xiaojun Jia

human_supports_claims: Two-stage semantic and conflict-aware filtering can defend RAG against corpus poisoning while preserving useful evidence. | Structured semantic extraction (entities, intent, relations) enables fine-grained detection of poisoned or conflicting retrieved documents. | Joint clustering plus semantic-graph filtering with conflict-aware inference reduces attack success rate across multiple LLMs and QA benchmarks.
human_rationale: SeCon-RAG proposes a two-stage defense (SCF + CAF) explicitly targeting corpus poisoning and prompt injection in RAG, combining clustering-based filtering, EIRE-guided semantic graph filtering, and inference-time conflict resolution across query/corpus/model knowledge. It is directly aligned with the survey's focus on robust RAG under unreliable evidence, providing both a security-integrity defense and an action-control-adjacent mechanism for resolving knowledge conflicts. The NeurIPS 2025 venue, evaluation across five LLMs and three QA datasets, and comparison with TrustRAG/AstuteRAG/InstructRAG make it a strong backbone citation for the security/defense section.
human_caveat: Relies on a small manually curated set of verified clean documents and multiple LLM calls, which may limit scalability and reproducibility; code availability is stated but artifact link is not clearly verified.

title: ReliabilityRAG: Effective and Provably Robust Defense for RAG-based Web-Search
authors: Zeyu Shen and Basileal Imana and Tong Wu and Chong Xiang and Prateek Mittal and Aleksandra Korolova

actual_contribution: NeurIPS 2025 paper; MIS-based contradiction graph using NLI plus weighted sample-and-aggregate; provable robustness against bounded corpus corruption with reliability/rank signals.
human_supports_claims: Reliability-aware document filtering using contradiction graphs and Maximum Independent Set provides provable robustness against bounded retrieval corruption in RAG | Leveraging retriever-provided ranking or cardinal reliability signals enables a defense-in-depth approach against prompt injection and corpus poisoning attacks | Weighted sample-and-aggregate frameworks can scale robust RAG defenses to larger retrieval sets while preserving robustness guarantees
human_rationale: This NeurIPS 2025 paper proposes ReliabilityRAG, a defense framework against adversarial attacks on RAG retrieval corpora using NLI-based contradiction detection and Maximum Independent Set selection that prioritizes higher-ranked documents. It provides both provable robustness guarantees and empirical evaluation against prompt injection and corpus poisoning, comparing favorably to RobustRAG, AstuteRAG, and InstructRAG on QA and long-form generation tasks. The work directly addresses robust RAG under unreliable/adversarial evidence and is a strong venue-backbone citation for the security/integrity perspective with explicit attention to retrieval reliability signals.
human_caveat: Defense effectiveness depends on NLI model accuracy and assumes bounded corruption; the consistent-majority assumption may not hold for ambiguous queries, and code was not released at submission time.

human_supports_claims: Mechanistic interventions on FFN activations can mitigate over-reliance on parametric memory and improve contextual faithfulness in RAG. | Benchmarks like CoFaithfulQA enable evaluation of LLM faithfulness under realistic conflicts between internal knowledge and accurate retrieved evidence.
human_rationale: ParamMute identifies a subset of mid-to-deep FFN layers causally implicated in unfaithful RAG generation and suppresses them, combined with preference optimization to calibrate the model toward retrieved evidence. It also introduces CoFaithfulQA, a benchmark built from six QA datasets that captures realistic context-vs-memory conflicts, and reports results on ConFiQA and FaithEval. This directly contributes to the survey's themes of faithfulness, knowledge conflict, and grounding under retrieved evidence, making it a strong main-text citation for the model evidence use perspective.
human_caveat: Evaluation focuses on QA settings with text contexts and a limited set of backbone models; mechanism-level claims about UA-FFNs may not generalize to all architectures or modalities.

title: To Trust or Not to Trust? Enhancing Large Language Models' Situated Faithfulness to External Contexts
authors: Yukun Huang and Sanxing Chen and Hongyi Cai and Bhuwan Dhingra
benchmark_or_task: GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, Llama-3-8B; QA with paired correct/incorrect contexts across NaturalQA, TriviaQA, PopQA, FreshQA, ClashEval, RedditQA

human_supports_claims: LLMs often over-rely on external context regardless of factual accuracy, motivating situated faithfulness that dynamically balances internal knowledge with external evidence. | Self-guided and rule-based confidence reasoning, especially when trained via CR-DPO, can improve robustness to incorrect retrieved contexts and generalize across QA datasets including the new RedditQA benchmark of human-written misleading posts.
human_rationale: The paper directly addresses robust RAG under unreliable evidence by benchmarking LLMs under knowledge conflicts with both LLM-synthesized and human-written incorrect contexts (RedditQA), and proposes SCR, RCR, and CR-DPO methods to enhance situated faithfulness. It contributes a clear taxonomy of confidence reasoning strategies, an evaluation protocol (Acc_t, Acc_f, SF), and a new dataset with verified noisy contexts, all of which are core to a survey on robust RAG. Main-text citation under model_evidence_use is appropriate because the work centers on grounding, faithfulness, and knowledge conflict resolution rather than retrieval or security per se.
human_caveat: Focuses on short-form QA with a single context per instance; multi-document retrieval and long-form generation conflicts are not directly evaluated.

title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems

human_supports_claims: Defining and detecting context sufficiency is a key lens for diagnosing RAG failures under unreliable evidence. | LLMs frequently hallucinate rather than abstain when retrieved context is insufficient, motivating action-control mechanisms. | Selective generation combining sufficient-context signals with model confidence improves accuracy-coverage trade-offs in RAG.
human_rationale: The paper introduces a formal notion of sufficient context and an LLM-based autorater to classify (query, context) pairs, then uses it to diagnose RAG failures across multiple SOTA models and benchmarks. It demonstrates that models hallucinate more than they abstain under insufficient context and proposes a selective generation method combining sufficiency and confidence signals to reduce hallucinations by 2-10%. This directly contributes both an evidence-quality diagnostic and an action-control mechanism central to a robust RAG survey, making it a backbone citation. The placement under evidence construction reflects the core sufficient-context contribution, though it could equally anchor action_control discussion.
human_caveat: Analysis is limited to QA datasets and does not cover summarization or multimodal RAG; autorater accuracy (93%) introduces some labeling noise in downstream claims.

title: Long-Context LLMs Meet RAG: Overcoming Challenges for Long Inputs in RAG
authors: Bowen Jin and Jinsung Yoon and Jiawei Han and Sercan O. Arik

actual_contribution: Analyzes hard-negative distraction in long-context RAG; proposes retrieval reordering and RAG-specific fine-tuning (implicit + intermediate reasoning) for robustness.
human_supports_claims: Increasing retrieved passage count for long-context LLMs follows an inverted-U pattern due to hard negatives, demonstrating the unreliability of larger retrieval contexts. | Retrieval reordering plus RAG-specific fine-tuning (implicit robustness and explicit relevance reasoning) improves robustness to hard negatives in long-context RAG. | Stronger retrievers can produce harder negatives that more severely mislead the generator, complicating the use of precision/recall as adequacy metrics.
human_rationale: This ICLR 2025 paper systematically diagnoses how hard negatives degrade long-context RAG performance and proposes a training-free reordering method plus two fine-tuning strategies (implicit robustness and explicit intermediate-reasoning relevance identification). It directly speaks to the survey's themes of unreliable evidence (noisy/hard-negative passages), evidence ordering, and robust generator behavior in a long-context scenario. The main:modality placement fits its long-context RAG focus, and it also offers strong cross-cutting evidence for evidence-construction and model-evidence-use sections.
human_caveat: Experiments focus on QA-style benchmarks with Wikipedia/PubMed corpora and a limited set of retrievers/LLMs; some claims (e.g., why Gemini-1.5-Pro is more robust) remain speculative.

title: FaithEval: Can Your Language Model Stay Faithful to Context, Even If "The Moon is Made of Marshmallows"
authors: Yifei Ming and Senthil Purushwalkam and Shrey Pandit and Zixuan Ke and Xuan-Phi Nguyen and Caiming Xiong and Shafiq Joty
benchmark_or_task: No retriever; 18 chat LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5, Llama-3, Gemma-2, Phi-3, Mistral, Command R) on provided contexts
metrics_reported_or_relevant: Strict and non-strict accuracy across three tasks
actual_contribution: ICLR 2025 benchmark of 4.9K samples across unanswerable/inconsistent/counterfactual contexts evaluating contextual faithfulness in RAG.
human_supports_claims: Contextual faithfulness of LLMs degrades sharply under unanswerable, inconsistent, and counterfactual evidence, even for state-of-the-art systems. | Dedicated benchmarks with multi-paragraph noisy contexts are needed to disentangle factuality from faithfulness in RAG evaluation. | Larger model size does not reliably translate into improved faithfulness under unreliable retrieved evidence.
human_rationale: FaithEval is an ICLR 2025 benchmark specifically designed to test LLM faithfulness under three classes of unreliable evidence (unanswerable, inconsistent, counterfactual) that directly mirror real-world RAG retrieval failures. With 4.9K validated samples across 10 source datasets and evaluation of 18 proprietary/open models, plus analyses of CoT, decoding strategies, and sycophancy from task-specific instructions, it provides a venue-backbone evaluation reference for a robust-RAG survey. It belongs in the evaluation section as a primary benchmark for contextual faithfulness under noisy/conflicting/missing evidence.
human_caveat: Focused on QA-style multi-paragraph text contexts; does not cover multimodal, agentic, or adversarial poisoning attacks, and counterfactual contexts are synthetic which may bias difficulty.

title: Controlling Risk of Retrieval-augmented Generation: A Counterfactual Prompting Framework
authors: Lu Chen and Ruqing Zhang and Jiafeng Guo and Yixing Fan and Xueqi Cheng

human_supports_claims: Counterfactual prompting that perturbs retrieval quality and usage can elicit RAG confidence signals for selective abstention. | Risk-aware metrics (risk, carefulness, alignment, coverage) complement EM/F1 for evaluating RAG abstention under noisy evidence. | RAG models suffer overconfidence on noisy retrieved passages, motivating dedicated risk-control mechanisms beyond LLM-only calibration.
human_rationale: The paper proposes a counterfactual prompting framework that induces a RAG model to reconsider answers under hypothesized poor retrieval quality or improper usage, then keeps or discards outputs based on answer stability. It introduces an RC-RAG benchmark and four risk-aware metrics (risk, carefulness, alignment, coverage) tailored to abstention under unreliable evidence, evaluating on NQ and TriviaQA with Mistral and ChatGPT. This directly supports the action-control axis of the survey (uncertainty, abstention, refusal in RAG) and offers a concrete method and evaluation protocol for unreliable retrieval contexts.
human_caveat: Limited to factoid QA in a zero-shot setting; the two latent factors are human-defined and fusion is heuristic, so generalization to multi-hop, long-form, or multimodal RAG is unverified.

human_supports_claims: RAG knowledge bases and agent long-term memory can be poisoned with <0.1% malicious instances to reliably trigger adversarial actions while preserving benign utility. | Constrained trigger optimization that maps triggered queries to a unique, compact embedding region transfers across dense retrievers and resists perplexity-based and rephrasing defenses. | Backdoor and poisoning threats are especially severe for RAG-based agents in safety-critical domains such as autonomous driving and healthcare.
human_rationale: AgentPoison is a NeurIPS 2024 paper that introduces the first backdoor attack specifically targeting RAG-based LLM agents by poisoning their memory or knowledge base, providing a novel constrained optimization to ensure malicious demonstrations are retrieved for triggered queries. It directly illustrates how unreliable/manipulated evidence stores can compromise RAG pipelines and induce adversarial agent actions, making it core material for the survey's security/integrity discussion of unreliable evidence. The empirical evaluation across three real agents, transferability analyses, and defense study give it strong evidentiary value for main-text discussion. The main caveat is that it assumes white-box access to the embedder for trigger optimization, though transferability mitigates this.

human_supports_claims: RAGTruth provides a large-scale word-level hallucination corpus tailored to RAG, enabling fine-grained evaluation of unsupported or conflicting outputs given retrieved evidence. | Fine-tuning a smaller LLM on RAGTruth yields hallucination detection competitive with GPT-4 prompt-based methods and can be used to suppress hallucinations at inference time. | Benchmarking shows even with retrieved references, leading LLMs produce baseless or conflicting content, motivating dedicated detection and mitigation components in robust RAG pipelines.
human_rationale: The paper introduces a venue-published, large-scale word-level hallucination corpus specifically for RAG settings across QA, data-to-text, and summarization, with four hallucination types and detailed span annotations. It benchmarks multiple detection methods (prompting, SelfCheckGPT, LMvLM, fine-tuned Llama) and demonstrates that detectors can reduce hallucination rates substantially when used to select among candidate responses. This directly supports an evaluation-focused section on diagnosing unreliable evidence use and model unfaithfulness in RAG, making it a core benchmark resource for the survey.
human_caveat: Coverage is limited to three English tasks and six specific LLMs from 2023-era models; generalization of the fine-tuned detector to other domains, languages, or newer models is not validated.

title: Synchronous Faithfulness Monitoring for Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Generation

source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

human_supports_claims: Synchronous monitoring of decoding dynamics (likelihood, uncertainty, context influence, semantic alignment) enables accurate sentence-level faithfulness detection in long-form RAG. | Faithfulness-oriented decoding via backtracking and beam search improves the faithfulness-informativeness tradeoff over abstention, reranking, and contrastive decoding. | Lightweight aggregators over complementary signals can generalize across tasks and models for trustworthy RAG.
human_rationale: The paper proposes SYNCHECK, a fine-grained faithfulness monitor that aggregates multiple decoding-time signals to detect unfaithful sentences in RAG outputs, plus FOD which uses these signals to guide beam search for more faithful generation. This directly addresses how models use retrieved evidence and how to detect and correct unreliable/unfaithful generation, which is central to robust RAG under unreliable evidence. It is appropriate for the main faithfulness/grounding section because it both characterizes failure modes and provides an actionable intervention mechanism. The work is venue-published (EMNLP 2024) with released code and benchmarks.
human_caveat: The method assumes sentence-level granularity and adds inference latency from extra forward passes; gains depend on a trained aggregator and may vary across larger or differently-tuned RALMs.

title: On the Vulnerability of Applying Retrieval-Augmented Generation within Knowledge-Intensive Application Domains

human_supports_claims: Dense retrievers used in domain-specific RAG are universally vulnerable to corpus poisoning that appends targeted content to attacker-chosen queries, with high top-K retrieval success across corpora, retrievers, and queries. | An orthogonal augmentation property of dense retrievers explains why poisoned concatenated documents retain high similarity to queries, motivating distribution-aware (Mahalanobis-style) detection defenses that outperform L2-norm baselines.
human_rationale: The paper provides a large-scale empirical study (225 setups in medical Q&A plus legal Q&A) showing dense retrievers can be reliably manipulated via concatenation-based poisoning, and offers a mechanistic explanation via the orthogonal augmentation property and low query-document similarity. It then proposes a shrinkage-regularized Mahalanobis detector that achieves near-perfect detection across attacks including PoisonedRAG. These are directly aligned with the survey's security/integrity and unreliable-evidence themes, making it a main citation under the security perspective with domain-specific scenario coverage.
human_caveat: Focus is mainly on retrieval-stage poisoning detection; downstream LLM generation robustness and adaptive attackers against the proposed detector are not deeply evaluated.

human_supports_claims: Adaptive retrieval methods that decide when to invoke retrieval require careful evaluation, and vanilla prompting is insufficient for guiding LLMs to make reliable retrieval decisions. | Benchmarks targeting knowledge absent from LLMs can isolate the evaluation of retrieval necessity decisions in adaptive RAG. | In-context demonstrations with time awareness can improve adaptive retrieval without calibration or additional training.
human_rationale: This ACL Findings 2024 paper introduces RetrievalQA, a benchmark of 1,271 short-form QA items whose answers are not in LLM parametric knowledge, enabling clean evaluation of adaptive retrieval decisions. It systematically compares calibration-based (e.g., Self-RAG threshold tuning) and model-based (vanilla prompting) ARAG approaches and proposes TA-ARE, a simple ICL-based method. The work is directly relevant to the action-control axis of robust RAG (when to retrieve, abstention, adaptive routing) and also contributes evaluation insight, making main_cite under main:control appropriate.

human_supports_claims: Neuron-level attribution can guide scalable poisoning of RAG external knowledge, exposing a new attack surface beyond surface-level prompt manipulation. | Knowledge conflict between parametric memory and retrieved evidence is exploitable via targeted activation of context-sensitive neurons, with attack success exceeding 90% across multiple LLMs and QA datasets. | Existing RAG poisoning defenses must consider internal representation dynamics, not just retrieval-level filtering, to address sophisticated genetic-optimization attacks.
human_rationale: This NeurIPS 2025 paper introduces NeuroGenPoisoning, an attack framework that combines neuron attribution (via Integrated Gradients) with genetic optimization to craft adversarial external knowledge that overrides LLM parametric memory in RAG settings. It directly addresses the unreliable-evidence threat model central to robust RAG by demonstrating scalable poisoning under knowledge conflict, with rigorous comparison to PoisonedRAG and explicit mechanistic analysis of poison-responsive neurons. Belongs in the security/integrity section as a key attack baseline informing the survey's discussion of RAG vulnerabilities and defense requirements. Risk of overclaim is minor since results are empirical on open-source LLMs and white-box attribution access is assumed.
human_caveat: Requires white-box attribution access (intermediate neuron activations), limiting realistic threat scope; black-box extension is future work.

human_supports_claims: Explicit relevance-assessment modules integrated into RAG architectures can mitigate LLM susceptibility to irrelevant or noisy retrieved documents. | Bi-granularity (coarse binary plus fine-grained preference) relevance supervision combined with noise-resistant training improves adaptive use of parametric versus external knowledge. | Relevance-aware generation enables knowledge-consistency verification between parametric and retrieved evidence for more reliable answer selection.
human_rationale: REAR adds an explicit relevance-assessment module to an LLM-based RAG pipeline and trains it with bi-granularity relevance fusion plus noise-resistant objectives so the model can adaptively rely on internal or external knowledge depending on document reliability. This directly addresses the survey's core question of how LLMs should behave under unreliable retrieved evidence, with quantitative gains on four open-domain QA benchmarks and explicit comparisons to Self-RAG and RobustLM. It is a venue-published EMNLP 2024 paper with code, making it a strong main-text reference in the model-evidence-use lineage. Overclaim risk is moderate: results are limited to open-domain QA and document-level (not sentence/token-level) relevance.
human_caveat: Evaluation is restricted to open-domain QA at document granularity; generalization to other knowledge-intensive tasks and finer-grained evidence is untested.

human_supports_claims: Adaptive contrastive decoding can dynamically balance parametric and retrieved knowledge based on entropy changes to mitigate the influence of noisy contexts in RAG. | Fixed-weight contrastive decoding methods (CAD, MICD) degrade under noisy retrieval, motivating uncertainty-aware adaptive weighting for robust grounding.
human_rationale: The paper proposes ACD, a decoding-time method that adjusts the contrastive weight between context-conditioned and parametric logits using entropy reduction as a signal of context informativeness, specifically targeting noisy retrieved contexts in open-domain QA. It directly addresses how models use retrieved evidence under unreliable conditions, making it a strong fit for the model_evidence_use section of a robust RAG survey. The empirical contrast against CAD and MICD across LLaMA/Mistral and three QA datasets provides useful evidence of robustness trade-offs between gold and noisy retrieval. Overclaim risk is limited to short-form QA and base (non-aligned) models, as the authors acknowledge.
human_caveat: Evaluated only on short-form open-domain QA with base LLMs; behavior under instruction-tuned models and long-form generation is untested.
